messages:
olivia: quick heads-up — after the merge from @max (c8f1b2) i'm seeing a p95 decode latency jump on canary. not huge but consistent across short-seq traffic. anyone else seeing this?

sam: yup saw it around 09:12. p95 went from ~28ms -> ~46ms on 8 GPU pool.

max: i pushed the warmup-throttle tweak to reduce kernel churn when kv cache cold-starts. thought it was net positive — weird it regresses decode p95.

jin: put together a quick perf snapshot:
```
# workload: shortseq=8, batch-target=32
before merge: decode p95=27.8ms, tokens/sec=5200
after merge:  decode p95=46.1ms, tokens/sec=5100
CPU % and memcpy spikes aligned with attn kernel selection events
```

laura: did CI perf compare run for the commit?

deploy-bot: perf-ci: perf/regressions/shortseq: baseline=28.1ms current=45.9ms (+63.4%), job=canary-042

olivia: thanks jin. can someone bisect locally? suspect kernel chooser now favors attn-transform path during warmup, causing extra kernel swaps for short sequences.

sam: i ran a narrow bisect: toggling warmup-throttle off locally reverts to baseline. toggled commit a9d7f3 (warmup-throttle) on/off and saw p95 flip.

max: hm, i added a heuristic to delay kernel switch until kv warmup hits threshold — intended to avoid tiny early kernels, but maybe it defers an optimal fused kernel and forces decode into slower fallback.

jin: captured a trace of kernel load events (timestamps are relative):
```
0ms  -> select kernel A (small-attn)
5ms  -> select kernel B (transformer-fused)
7ms  -> evict kernel A
9ms  -> reselect kernel A (because seq len changed)
... many kernel load/unload syscalls, memcpy spikes ~5-12ms window
```

laura: could be thrash between two kernels when warmup-threshold sits in the middle. if selector oscillates we get repeated memcpy + launch overhead.

sam: reproduce steps i used:
1) run canary shortseq sim (same seed)
2) capture perf trace: ./tools/perf-trace --job canary-042 --span 60s > trace.json
3) set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_WARMUP_THRESHOLD=0 to disable and re-run -> p95 back to 28ms

olivia: ok plan: max, revert warmup-throttle change from main for canary hold. jin/sam, pls collect detailed trace + kernellog and a minimal repro script we can run in CI. laura, open a rollout-blocker ticket and attach perf CI link.

max: will cut the revert PR in a few mins. note: the change helps long-seq throughput by ~4% in internal tests; we need to find an approach that preserves that without shortseq penalty.

jin: attaching quick grep of logs showing selection flip pattern (excerpt):
```
[selector] seq_len=8 -> choose kernel small-attn
[selector] kv_warmup=3 -> postpone fused-kernel
[selector] kv_warmup=6 -> choose fused-kernel
[selector] seq_len=8 -> choose small-attn
```

sam: also saw repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree around those flips in the trace which maps to memcpy churn.

deploy-bot: deploy:revert PR #2892 opened by max -> status: draft -> assign to eng-runtime oncall

olivia: if we revert, let's also add a unit test exercising the transient warmup window (simulate kv warmup counts) so this doesn't regress again. max: please include profiling knobs so we can A/B in CI.

max: ack. i'll include a canary matrix: warmup=0, warmup=3, warmup=6 and add perf assertions for shortseq p95.

laura: ticket created: RD-INF-4678 (rollout-blocker) with perf CI link and summary. tagging legal/regulatory? no. tagging infra-team for CI artifact storage.

olivia: thanks all. if revert lands and canary stabilizes we'll rework selection logic to prefer kernel stability over marginal longseq gains for shortseq-heavy routes. moving to canary-hold until next update. :eyes: 

max: reverted and pushed PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2892 :thumbsup: 

sam: rerun canary job now.

deploy-bot: perf-ci: rerun job canary-042 -> current p95=28.3ms (within baseline)

olivia: nice, closing the immediate roll out. follow-ups: 1) detailed perf diff for longseq vs shortseq 2) selector hysteresis (avoid oscillation) 3) CI test matrix. i'll track in RD-INF-4678.
